title: The real Astra 6 Effort
author: Beginning-Sign1916
selftext: Hope everyone can really share the effort used for building out a completely scratch game with high res quality assets/graphics. I am trying out the Medium and High so far on my Plus plan and I don't mind upgrading to the 20x plan just that will that really work way better in getting my project out with ease on the assets generating and design. On a really curious side has anyone tried the Ultra effort?

comments.author: shady101852
comments.body:
ive been running Astra on max working on a brand new game. So far the goal has been running for 3 days 17 hours and still going, but keep in mind this is with a few usage resets and this is not the only project i am working on. I think you can easily go through 20-50% of your weekly usage with Astra on the 20x plans in 24 hours depending on workload.

Ultra is not a reasoning level, it encourages the model to use subagents (which will lead to more usage consumption). I personally never use it for this reason.

Max is the highest reasoning level.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
I need to do things very differently, but from what I see, you'll generally want to set up:

* MCP with Unreal. Unity is viable too, but stuff like Metahuman and the whole breadth of high-quality assets provided for Unreal makes for quicker progress and more impressive results. Unreal is what's usually used in those jaw-dropping showcases, althrough theoritically Unity 
* MCP with Blender for making your own 3D models. Focus on props here, for more complicated stuff you need more knowledge on how this works.
* A version control system, which is a step most vibers new to coding are skipping because it requires some learning to not make mistakes. Although they can achieve great first results, they can lose all of their progress when making mistakes. If you project is small and the total assets won't be more than single digit Gigabytes in size, go for Git and Git LFS enabled. You'll need a different version control system like Perforce if you plan do have a bigger total asset size. If your fine with YOLO and risking everything every time you change something, you can of course skip that part.
* Try not doing everything with Astra, it just consumes too much usage (unless you are ready to spend lots of $$$). There are always some simpler task that a very economical model like gpt 5.6 luna on very high/max reasoning can.
* Have a minimum of non-AI automated gates that AI needs to run before proceeding with the next thing. For example, a linter statistically checking for recommended rules.
* The agents needs to be instructed to keep record of their progress in an .md files that is well visibile to you and reviewed regularly. Don't let it track everything in a place you don't usually look at, like agent memory.
* You'll want to use the features made for long-term horizon tasks for your respective AI agent so it doesn't stop working too early after finishing a bit. For codex that would be using \`/goal\`.

One more weird thing I have to say on the topic is that there is ironically a sweetspot for automated tests that slow everything down, because it impedes progress when they are too slow, but if they take just the right amount of extra time, then it can happen that you slide right into the next 5h usage window and thus your session won't be interrupted because you didn't reach usage limits due to the slow automated tests. Sounds a bit retarded, of course, but I found that too be somewhat effective in practice. In fact, I'm thinking of building a usage-aware sleep time into my verification step to achieve the same.

replies.author: heavy-minium
replies.body: Oh and btw, Astra high is not really worth it. On coding benchmark, it seems the improvement is not worth it. Medium is just fine as your maximum reasoning level and will consume less usage.

comments.author: EssayUnique6037
comments.body: I am currently building a burger shop simulator and have used Opus, Fable and now Astra and i think Astra has the best understanding of the assets when its building or fixing them in Blender via MCP. I have tried building things only via pictures from Google but i think what works better is using the ImageGen via Chat or directly invoking it, so that it can create its own reference sheets with different angles. I have bought a few assets and use them like a design guideline to create the ones no one has designed so i stay within the same design pattern. Works good so far. Not tried it with characters or animations so far only static assets. Style is stylized no low poly or high realism.
